Simulate torque-driven rigid-body dynamics

Source: R/dynamics.R
robot_simulate.Rd

Integrates \(\ddot q = ABA(q, \dot q, \tau(t, q, \dot q))\) with deSolve::ode(). This is a dynamic simulation of the rigid-body model only: joint limits, friction, contact and impacts are not modeled, and the result is not a high-fidelity physics simulation. Energy drift in an unforced conservative simulation measures integrator error, not model error; tighten rtol and atol to reduce it.

robot_simulate(
  robot,
  q0,
  qd0 = NULL,
  times,
  torque = NULL,
  gravity = c(0, 0, -9.81),
  f_ext = NULL,
  method = "lsoda",
  rtol = 1e-08,
  atol = 1e-10
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model with inertial parameters.

q0, qd0

Initial positions and velocities.

times

Output times (seconds), increasing.

torque

A function function(t, q, qd) returning joint efforts, or NULL for zero torque.

gravity

Gravity vector in world coordinates.

f_ext

Optional named list of external wrenches.

method

Integration method passed to deSolve::ode().

rtol, atol

Integration tolerances.

Value

A robot_trajectory with time, q, qd and qdd.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar1")
sim <- robot_simulate(robot, q0 = 0.5, qd0 = 0, times = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
                      gravity = c(0, -9.81, 0))
tail(sim$q, 1)
#>          joint1
#> [11,] -3.555636
